draft.title: Variables and hypotheses
card: the variable the researcher changes or manipulates. It is the suspected cause.
the variable the researcher measures. It is the suspected effect, and it may change because of the independent variable.
A hypothesis predicts how the independent variable will affect the dependent variable.
A good hypothesis also names the population, which is the group the results are meant to apply to, such as Year 10 students.
draft.remember: Change the IV, measure the DV, and predict the link for a named population.

a.q: A researcher gives some students a 10 minute walk and others none, then measures their scores on a concentration test. What is the dependent variable?
opts: Scores on the concentration test
Whether a student took the 10 minute walk
The length of the walk in minutes
The group of students who took part
a.why: The test scores are what the researcher measures, so they are the dependent variable. The walk is what the researcher changes, so it is the independent variable, which is the most tempting wrong answer.
a.clue: Which one is measured at the end?

b.q: Which hypothesis names the independent variable, the dependent variable and the population?
opts: Adults who sleep 8 hours will recall more words than those who sleep 4
Sleep will be changed for adults, and word recall will be measured
Adults who sleep less may differ in how well they do things
Sleep length will be varied to see how it affects memory in people
b.why: The first option predicts how sleep (IV) affects words recalled (DV) for adults. The second only describes the method, with no prediction. The third is vague about the DV, and the fourth names no population.
b.clue: Look for a prediction that links both variables and names the group.

b.q: A researcher changes how long adults sleep, then counts how many words they recall. Which hypothesis predicts how the IV affects the DV for a named population?
opts: Adults who sleep for longer will recall more words
Sleep will be changed for adults and word recall measured
Adults who recall more words will sleep for longer
Longer sleep will lead to more words being recalled
b.why: Saying adults who sleep for longer will recall more words predicts how sleep (the IV) affects recall (the DV) and names adults as the population. The statement about longer sleep leading to more words recalled is tempting, but it names no population. The other two either describe the method with no prediction or treat recall as the cause.
b.clue: Check for a prediction, the right cause and a named group.
